newsitem.title: INDIA: India grieves for haj victims.
newsitem.headline: India grieves for haj victims.

text.p: India expressed shock and grief on Wednesday over the death of more than 200 Moslem pilgrims, many of them Indians, in a blaze in Saudi Arabia.

"The prime minister has expressed deep grief and anguish over...the devastating fire in which a large number of pilgrims from India and other countries lost their lives," said a statement from Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's office.
More than 200 Moslem pilgrims were killed in the fire, triggered by a cooking gas cylinder and fanned by high winds, which swept through a sea of tents near the holy city of Mecca on Tuesday.

Most of the victims were reported to be from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. They were among some two million Moslems from 100 countries gathering for the annual haj pilgrimage, which reaches its climax on Wednesday.
India's ambassador in Riyadh, Mohammad Hamad Ansari, said on Tuesday that more than 100 Indian pilgrims were believed to have died.
"The death of our pilgrims has caused me immense personal grief and anguish. My heartfelt condolences are with the relatives of the deceased," Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said in a statement.

A Foreign Ministry official in charge of an emergency haj unit set up to handle enquiries said two tents sheltering Indians were gutted in the fire, but that no figure for the number of Indians who were killed was yet available.
"Their camp number 59, which had roughly 100 Indians in it, was completely charred, but we can't say how many people exactly died," said the official.
"Identification of the dead will commence on April 19, when the pilgrims come back from Mount Arafat."
Praying at Mount Arafat, where the Prophet Mohammad gave his last sermon 14 centuries ago, marks the climax of haj.
Junior Home Minister Mohammad Maqbool Dar, who was leading a goodwill delegation of 14 Indian lawmakers to Mecca, said none of them were injured in the fire.
A team of Foreign Ministry officials was to fly to Riyadh later on Wednesday to help coordinate evacuations and provide aid to survivors and relatives of the deceased, officials said.
Moslems make up for nearly 12 percent of India's population of 936 million.
